topic: .NET tracer on Windows Server causing Windows job services to fail after machine-wide COR_ENABLE_PROFILING
environment: Separate Windows services (jobs) running outside IIS
symptom_pattern: After a Windows Server OS upgrade, tracer data was missing. Setting COR_ENABLE_PROFILING=1 and restarting IIS restored APM traces for the IIS app. After that, separate Windows job services outside IIS no longer started, or showed as Running but could not run jobs. Uninstalling the Agent and tracer made the jobs work again.
root_cause: COR_ENABLE_PROFILING=1 was set at machine (global) scope. The .NET runtime then tried to load the tracer into every .NET process on the host, including the job services outside IIS, which broke them. Later the variable appeared to have been set again without COR_PROFILER, leaving an inconsistent profiling state. The thread does not establish what re-applied it.
resolution_path: On a call, found COR_ENABLE_PROFILING=1 set at machine level on the affected server
Removed it with [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable, after which the jobs started
Customer later reported the services showed Running but no jobs would run, with an error in the event logs
The screenshot showed COR_ENABLE_PROFILING set but COR_PROFILER not, so the removed variable had been set again
Uninstalled the .NET tracer and restarted IIS
Checked whether COR_ENABLE_PROFILING, COR_PROFILER and COR_PROFILER_PATH were set at Machine scope, and removed them if so
Restarted the job services, rebooting if necessary, and tested the jobs
Reinstalled the tracer and restarted IIS
Customer confirmed the issue was resolved
info_needed: Whether COR_ENABLE_PROFILING, COR_PROFILER and COR_PROFILER_PATH are set at Machine scope
Whether the issue is on the same server troubleshot during the call
Whether the event log error appears at the Windows job level or in the IIS application
Whether a group policy re-adds COR_ENABLE_PROFILING=1
Whether another profiler or APM agent is installed on the server

tse_approach.summary: The engineer clarified the IIS-plus-job-services setup and held a live call to reproduce the issue. That call found the machine-wide COR_ENABLE_PROFILING variable. When the problem came back, they spotted the inconsistent variable state in the customer's screenshot and gave a clean-up procedure.
steps: Scheduled a Zoom troubleshooting call during the customer's downtime window
Found the machine-level COR_ENABLE_PROFILING=1 on the call and gave the command to remove it
Sent a follow-up with the command and the relevant public doc section
Reviewed the customer's screenshot and noticed COR_PROFILER was missing while COR_ENABLE_PROFILING was set
Gave ordered steps: uninstall tracer, check and clear the three COR_ variables, restart services, reinstall tracer
Asked about group policy, a second profiler, and where the error appeared
Marked the ticket solved after the customer confirmed
key_questions: Is the issue on the same server troubleshot during the call?
Did the error event appear in the Windows jobs or in an IIS application?
Is a group policy adding COR_ENABLE_PROFILING=1 again?
Is any other profiler or APM agent installed?
